g.text: Two dunes in plan view (same scale) and their long-term winds
Long-term sand-moving winds: % of time from each direction
(bars point to where the wind comes from)
A: four arms radiate from a central peak, each about 300 m long:
a star dune, consistent with winds from many directions.
B: one long, narrow crest: a linear (seif-type) dune. South-west
and south-east winds give a net drift towards the north, along
Scale: B is about 800 m long but only 40 m wide (20:1); A is
about 600 m across in several directions. Shape and proportion
classify them, not colour or a place name.
